title: The Standing of an Enrolment and What a Withdrawal Releases
content:
An enrolment on the Keyturn Host Protection Plan that has drawn enough accepted claims to stand in front of a reviewer has part of a withdrawal's release retained.

- Where the claims accepted on the enrolment in the twelve months before reach the number the plan allows before the enrolment goes in front of a reviewer and a share stands unpaid on it, the release is taken at the marketplace's arrears release share of 95 percent.
- Where they reach that number and nothing stands unpaid, it is taken at the marketplace's reviewed-standing share of 98 percent.
- Where they do not reach that number, nothing is retained on that account.

### The number each plan publishes

| Plan | Claims allowed before review |
|---|---|
| Keyturn Shield 90 Host Plan | 2 |
| Keyturn Shield 85 Host Plan | 2 |
| Keyturn Shield 80 Host Plan | 3 |
| Keyturn Shield 75 Host Plan | 3 |
| Keyturn Shield 70 Host Plan | 4 |
| Keyturn Shield 60 Host Plan | 5 |

### Figures worked through (hypothetical)

On the Keyturn Shield 85 Host Plan, whose published number is 2, an enrolment with 1 accepted claim in the twelve months before retains nothing; with 2 accepted claims and a share standing unpaid it releases 95 percent of the figure, and with 2 accepted claims and nothing unpaid it releases 98 percent.

### Where the reading is taken from

The claims counted are the appraisals accepted on this enrolment within the twelve months before, and what stands unpaid is the amount owed by the host on the enrolment.
